clue.text: Birmingham’s home sweet home?

blocks.note: first meaning: the US state in which the American city of Birmingham stands
second meaning: the place hailed as 'sweet home' in a famous Lynyrd Skynyrd rock song title

explanation.surface: Fond words about Birmingham as the place someone loves to come home to.
explanation.walkthrough: A British solver thinks of the West Midlands, but there is a larger Birmingham in the American South; the song Sweet Home Alabama clinches it.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern US state contains the city of Birmingham and is the subject of the 1974 rock anthem about returning there.

clue.text: Look less English, put on the Spanish clobber

indicators.note: having less of something means a letter is taken away

blocks.note: to look a certain way is to appear so
E is the abbreviation for English; it is removed
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone trying to seem less English by dressing in Spanish gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look less English' seems to describe a disguise, but it is an instruction: a synonym of look loses its E. Clobber is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British slang for clothing or gear, and apparel is the formal word for garments worn.

clue.text: Unwind, relax with a lap dance and a game of darts here?

indicators.note: to unwind is to undo something coiled, so the letters are loosened and set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the article from 'a game', taken as written

explanation.surface: An evening of relaxing, a lap dance and some darts: a lads' night out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' of 'a game' does double duty in the fodder. Alexandra Palace, or Ally Pally, is a north London venue that hosts the world darts championship.
explanation.definitionFit: The professional world darts championship is staged each winter at this north London entertainment venue, so it is where darts is played.

clue.text: Swedish foursome that swings both ways?

definitions.text: Swedish foursome that swings both ways?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pop group of four from Sweden, with a saucy hint about their love lives
setter's reading: the band's name reads the same forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a Swedish group's private life.
explanation.walkthrough: The innuendo is a red herring: 'both ways' just means the name reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Swedish pop group consisted of four members, two couples, who won Eurovision in 1974.

clue.text: Old city against leader of Orthodox Church

indicators.note: the leader of a word is whatever comes at its head, its opening letter

blocks.note: anti means opposed to
the opening letter of this word
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An ancient city opposing the head of the Orthodox Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Orthodox Church' reads as a patriarch, but the leader is only the first letter, and Church stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a major ancient Hellenistic city in Syria, now Antakya in Turkey, and an early Christian centre.

clue.text: Mister Capello, so really entertaining when retired

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so the letters sit inside the words
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the surname, the whole of 'so', and the start of 'really'

explanation.surface: Addressing former England manager Fabio Capello as 'Mister', saying he was great fun in retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: Mister looks like a form of address for Capello, but it is the definition: a thing that produces mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray can turns liquid into a fine mist, so it is literally a mister in the device sense.

clue.text: In the morning, taking close companion for scuba, say

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: AM is ante meridiem, before noon
a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: Going diving in the morning with a close friend.
explanation.walkthrough: AM opens to hold CRONY. Scuba stands for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus, so it is a word built from initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba is a classic example of a word formed from initial letters and pronounced as a word itself.

clue.text: Timeless court case ready in Iran?

indicators.note: being without time means the abbreviation for time is dropped

blocks.note: a court case is a trial; its T is removed

explanation.surface: A never-ending court case in Iran is finally ready to start.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the abbreviation for time. 'Ready' is not an adjective here but British slang for cash, as in 'the readies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rial is the national currency of Iran, so it is the money, or readies, used there.

clue.text: Snap using telephoto to capture female boob

indicators.note: something that snaps breaks apart, so the letters are broken and remade
capturing something means taking it in, so a letter is held within

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A paparazzo zooming in for a revealing photo of a woman's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' and 'telephoto' suggest photography, but snap is the anagram signal. Boob is British slang for a blunder as well as the cheeky sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is an embarrassing mistake, and an accidental wrong word said aloud is one such verbal blunder.

clue.text: Chimney pot beginning to oxidise – such a pain

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: lum is a Scots and northern word for a chimney
to pot game is to shoot it, which is also to bag it
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A rusting chimney pot is a real nuisance for the householder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chimney pot' reads as one thing but splits in two. Pot as a verb means to shoot or capture, the same as bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is a painful condition of the lower back, so it is a particular kind of ache or pain.

clue.text: Britney Spears: I’m changing religious doctrine

indicators.note: when something is changing its form alters, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The pop star announcing that she is switching faiths.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of the pop star's name plus I'M makes exactly fifteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Presbyterianism is the theology and church government of Reformed Protestant churches run by elders, a body of religious teaching.

clue.text: Wander around the Eternal City, so to speak

indicators.note: speaking points to how words are pronounced rather than written

blocks.note: the Eternal City is the traditional nickname of the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Strolling about Rome as a tourist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian capital and the word for wandering are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to travel aimlessly over a wide area, the same as wandering about.

clue.text: Establish nothing’s in the kitty

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O
a kitty is a pool of money, a fund

explanation.surface: Discovering that the shared kitty is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' suggests a cat, but here it is a pot of pooled money.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an organisation is to set it up or bring it into being, which is to establish it.

clue.text: Piece of furniture, very fine article

blocks.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Admiring an excellent piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very fine article' reads as praise for the furniture but splits into three small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people, an item found in most living rooms.

clue.text: Help set up Railway Journal

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up turns it upwards so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: aid means help
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone helping to launch a railway magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railway Journal' reads like a magazine title, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a daily record of events and thoughts, which is what a personal journal is.

clue.text: Info on literary style

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
re means on or about, as in a memo

explanation.surface: Reading up on a particular kind of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category of artistic work such as crime fiction or romance, a kind or style of writing.

clue.text: Like a boisterous youth left his dad upset?

indicators.note: when something is upset it is knocked over and disordered

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rowdy teenager who walked out and left his father distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb about abandoning the father, but it supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddish describes the brash, rowdy behaviour associated with young men, the manner of a boisterous lad.

clue.text: Mum established boundaries for Rigoletto conductor

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its edges, its outer letters

blocks.note: ma is a word for mother
est. is the abbreviation for established
the first and last letters of the opera title

explanation.surface: A mother laying down the limits for the man conducting Verdi's opera Rigoletto.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera name invites musical thinking, but only its outermost letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is the respectful title for a distinguished conductor of orchestras or opera.

clue.text: Annoyance of Greek stuck in mountain range

indicators.note: being stuck inside something means being held within it

blocks.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
a mountain chain is a range

explanation.surface: A Greek hiker's frustration at being trapped in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: A range of mountains is also called a chain, which opens after its third letter to take the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is distress or vexation at having failed or been humiliated, a feeling of irritation.

clue.text: Colonel Gaddafi at the front wearing a certain scent

indicators.note: what sits at the front of a word is its first letter
whatever is worn goes around the wearer, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
the opening letter of the name
'a certain person' can be 'one'

explanation.surface: The Libyan dictator leading the way, doused in a particular perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonel Gaddafi' reads as one title, but it splits: the rank is abbreviated and only his initial is used, dressed in ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne, short for eau de Cologne, is a light perfume, so it is a fragrance or scent.

clue.text: Gwen turned up with temperature in A&E in gaol

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up flips it to read from the bottom
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature
A&E is accident and emergency, a hospital casualty department; just its letters

explanation.surface: Gwen arrives at casualty with a fever, while in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department. Newgate was London's notorious old prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a famous London prison for over seven centuries, so it is a particular jail.

clue.text: Upstart VP ran EU ragged

indicators.note: something ragged is torn and messy, so the letters are in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An upstart vice-president ran the European Union into the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran ... ragged' reads as an idiom for exhausting someone, but ragged alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a person of humble origins who has newly gained wealth or status, a social climber.

clue.text: Church revenue ahead of the curve?

blocks.note: pre means before
a curve in a road is a bend

explanation.surface: A church whose income is ahead of the curve, i.e. ahead of trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of the curve' is an idiom for being progressive, but it splits into a prefix and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A prebend is the stipend a canon draws from a cathedral's estates, a portion of ecclesiastical income.

clue.text: In court, going to get punished, highly motivated

definitions.text: In court, going to get punished

blocks.clueFragment: In court, going to get punished
blocks.note: first meaning: facing trial and due a penalty, as in being up before the judge
second meaning: keen and eager to take part

explanation.surface: A defendant awaiting sentence while also being very keen.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal British phrase means both 'in trouble and about to be dealt with' and 'enthusiastic and willing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers someone summoned to answer a charge and also, colloquially, someone eager and willing to do something.

clue.text: Boy bored by electronic heavy metal

indicators.note: something bored by a drill has another thing passing through its middle

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A teenager who finds electronic music and heavy metal tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' looks like a music genre alongside 'electronic', but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a dense, soft, grey chemical element, one of the heaviest common metals.

clue.text: Bird bowls Beth left completely uncovered

indicators.note: uncovering something strips away its outer layers, leaving only the inside

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
the name without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bird knocks Beth over and leaves her exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowls' looks like a verb, as in knocking someone over, but it is only fodder for its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, which is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Pack animal‘s run over

indicators.note: turning something over flips it so it reads the other way

blocks.note: to run, of water, is to flow

explanation.surface: A beast of burden has been knocked down by a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack animal' suggests a mule carrying loads; it is an animal that hunts in packs.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolves live and hunt in family groups called packs, so the wolf is the classic pack animal.

clue.text: About to get upset, Oscar’s forgotten horn

indicators.note: in a down clue, being upset turns something upside down
what is forgotten is left out

blocks.note: taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet; it is removed

explanation.surface: Someone about to be upset because Oscar has left his instrument behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to get upset' reads as 'nearly upset', but 'About' is the word turned over, then the O drops out.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is a large, low-pitched brass instrument, and brass instruments are loosely called horns.

clue.text: Starts to accept succubus is featured in your dreams

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A dreamer resigned to a seductive demon appearing in their sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: A succubus is a female demon said to visit men in dreams, which makes 'in your dreams' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive exclamations meaning that something will never happen, used to scorn an unlikely idea.

clue.text: Old lady, new LSU graduate that’s very sweet

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun

indicators.note: making something new means it is made over in a different form

blocks.note: gran is a grandmother
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grandma, a fresh graduate of Louisiana State University, is a real sweetie.
explanation.walkthrough: LSU is Louisiana State University; 'very sweet' sounds like praise for the gran but describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Granulated sugar is the common white table sugar in small grains, the substance that makes food taste sweet.

clue.text: Raise tax collected by European shelter

indicators.note: something collected by another is gathered up inside it

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
VAT is value added tax
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Raising a tax gathered by a European tax haven.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT, value added tax, is the British sales tax; 'shelter' is the lee, the side out of the wind, not a tax shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate something is to lift it to a higher position or level, which is what raising means.

clue.text: Most silly whim put back trial

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a fad is a passing craze or whim
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A foolish fancy that caused a trial to be postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back trial' reads as postponing a court case, but the putting back applies to the word before.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is informal British for foolish, so its superlative means the most foolish or silly.
